claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child Alex, who is 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether they are in approved education or training.

Could you please tell me if Alex is currently in full-time education or training? If so, what type of education or training are they in (for example, A-levels, a vocational course, or an apprenticeship)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in full-time education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that. A-levels at sixth form college counts as approved education, so that's a positive sign for eligibility.

Now I just need to confirm a few more details:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

Now, could you please confirm your responsibility for Alex? Specifically:

Does Alex live with you, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of Child Benefit (currently £25.60 per week for the eldest child) towards their upkeep (for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week in paid employment?
2. Does Alex receive any benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all - he's focused on his studies. And no, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **You live in the UK** – You're based in Manchester, meeting the residency requirement.

✅ **Alex is under 20 and in approved education** – Although Alex is 17 (over the usual age of 16), Child Benefit can continue up to age 20 if the child stays in approved education or training. A-levels at sixth form college qualifies as approved education.

✅ **You're responsible for Alex** – Alex lives with you at home.

✅ **No disqualifying factors** – Alex is not working 24+ hours per week and does not receive benefits in their own right.

You can apply for Child Benefit online or by post if you haven't already. Please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge, but you can still claim and choose whether to receive payments.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
